questions.q: A matrix is singular if its determinant is:
questions.explanation: Singular means |A| = 0, so it has no inverse.

questions.q: If a 3x3 matrix A has |A| = 5, what is |2A|?
If two rows of a determinant are identical, its value is:
questions.explanation: Identical rows or columns make the determinant zero.

questions.q: What is the determinant of the Identity matrix I?
questions.explanation: The product of the diagonal elements of I is always 1.

questions.q: The formula for A<sup class="sup">-1</sup> is:
questions.explanation: The inverse requires dividing the adjoint by the determinant.

questions.q: If |A| = 4 for a 3x3 matrix, what is |adj(A)|?
Cramer's Rule fails if the main determinant D is:
questions.explanation: Because Cramer's Rule involves division by D, it fails if D = 0.

questions.q: The determinant of a diagonal matrix is:
questions.explanation: For any triangular or diagonal matrix, |A| is the product of its main diagonal.
